title: Methods
explain: A method is a function with a receiver, written between `func` and the name. Use a value receiver to read data and a pointer receiver when the method must change it. Go lets you call both kinds on a variable without extra syntax.
exercise: Add a `Reset` method to Counter and a `String` method so `fmt.Println(c)` prints `Counter(2)`.
tip: Mixing value and pointer receivers on one type is confusing. If any method needs a pointer receiver, use pointer receivers for all of them.
